selector.rationale: Ovarian cancer is supported by elevated CA-125, PET-CT findings of FDG-avid thickening of bilateral adnexa, and hypermetabolic osteolytic lesions, despite ultrasound not showing masses or cysts, which could be due to early stage disease or limitations of the imaging modality.

rejected.label: abdominal tuberculosis
rejected.why: No specific evidence in the vignette supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Meigs syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with a benign ovarian tumor, ascites, and pleural effusion, but the vignette suggests malignancy

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While it can cause lymphadenopathy and pleural effusions, the presence of hypermetabolic osteolytic lesions and elevated CA-125 points more towards a malignant process

rejected.label: Pericardial Effusion due to Malignancy
rejected.why: This is a symptom rather than a primary diagnosis, and Ovarian cancer is a more specific diagnosis that explains the findings

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Although it is a close runner-up due to the presence of lymphadenopathy and hypermetabolic lesions, the specific findings pointing towards ovarian cancer (e.g., elevated CA-125, adnexal involvement) make it a less likely primary diagnosis
